docs.title: Welcome to the documentation of Epsilon
docs.text: Epsilon is a somatic SNV caller from Illumina WGS or WES data.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Install Epsilon from its repository:

git clone https://github.com/JakubLiu/Epsilon.git

After cloning the repository the following directory structure is present:

├── env.yaml
└── project/
    ├── Epsilon.smk
    ├── Epsilon_config.yaml
    ├── run_epsilon.sh
    └── scripts/
        ├── Epsilon_Fit.sh
        ├── Epsilon_MakeData.sh
        ├── Epsilon_MakeData_call.sh
        ├── Epsilon_call.sh
        ├── call.R
        ├── extract_features_alt_generic.py
        ├── extract_features_alt_generic_call.py
        ├── extract_features_alt_specific.py
        ├── extract_features_alt_specific_call.py
        ├── fit.R
        ├── make_data_alt_generic.py
        ├── make_data_alt_generic_call.py
        ├── make_data_alt_specific.py
        ├── make_data_alt_specific_call.py
        └── remove_germlines.R

In order to satisfy all dependencies please execute the following commands:

cd Epsilon
conda env create -f env.yaml
conda activate Epsilon_env

docs.title: Epsilon and Slurm
docs.text:
It is possible to submit the different sub-steps of the Epsilon workflow as separate Slurm jobs, in order to speed up computation.

Assuming that a configuration profile is set up as shown in:

https://snakemake.readthedocs.io/en/v7.19.1/executing/cli.html#profiles

and assuming that you are located in the project/ directory (and your configuration file is called Epsilon_config.yaml), Epsilon can be submitted as a Slurm job with the following command:

snakemake --snakefile Epsilon.smk \
          --configfile Epsilon_config.yaml \
          --profile <your profile> \
          --jobs <number of jobs>

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
In order to run Epsilon, the scripts/ directory must be located in the project directory alongside Epsilon.smk, Epsilon_config.yaml and run_espilon.sh. Assuming our project is called genome a valid directory structure would be:

└── genome
    ├── Epsilon.smk
    ├── Epsilon_config.yaml
    ├── run_epsilon.sh
    └── scripts
        ├── Epsilon_Fit.sh
        ├── Epsilon_MakeData.sh
        ├── Epsilon_MakeData_call.sh
        ├── Epsilon_call.sh
        ├── call.R
        ├── extract_features_alt_generic.py
        ├── extract_features_alt_generic_call.py
        ├── extract_features_alt_specific.py
        ├── extract_features_alt_specific_call.py
        ├── fit.R
        ├── make_data_alt_generic.py
        ├── make_data_alt_generic_call.py
        ├── make_data_alt_specific.py
        ├── make_data_alt_specific_call.py
        └── remove_germlines.R

Assuming that the user is located in genome/ the way to run Epsilon is:

./run_epsilon.sh --config <name of config file> --jobs <number of parallel jobs>

The config file defines all the input and output files as well as all the parameters of Epsilon. The structure is the following:

reference_genome:
negative_control_bamlist:
loci_list:
alt_mode: "generic"
nranks: 1
max_noise_level: 0.05
tumor_path:
matched_normal_path:
calling_loci_list:
variant_calling_model: "binomial"
fdr_method: "BH"
alpha: 0.05
prior: 0.3
posterior_cutoff: 0.5
output_vcf: "output.vcf"

For a detailed description of all the elements of the config file please look at the Config file structure subpage.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
After a succesful run, the directory tree will look like this:

project/
├── Epsilon.smk
├── Epsilon_config.yaml
├── run_epsilon.sh
├── scripts/
│   ├── Epsilon_Fit.sh
│   ├── Epsilon_MakeData.sh
│   ├── Epsilon_MakeData_call.sh
│   ├── Epsilon_call.sh
│   ├── call.R
│   ├── extract_features_alt_generic.py
│   ├── extract_features_alt_generic_call.py
│   ├── extract_features_alt_specific.py
│   ├── extract_features_alt_specific_call.py
│   ├── fit.R
│   ├── make_data_alt_generic.py
│   ├── make_data_alt_generic_call.py
│   ├── make_data_alt_specific.py
│   ├── make_data_alt_specific_call.py
│   └── remove_germlines.R
├── data/
├── error_model/
│   └── error_model.rds
├── tumor_data/
│   ├── matched_normal_data.txt
│   └── tumor_data.txt
├── unfiltered_variant_calls/
│   ├── matched_normal.vcf
│   └── tumor.vcf
└── filtered_variant_calls/
    └── tumor.vcf

The final output vcf file is the filtered_variant_calls/tumor.vcf file.

docs.title: meaning
docs.text: The unadjusted level of statistical significance, only applicable if the variant_calling_model is set to binomial.

docs.title: meaning
docs.text: Defines if any non-reference allele is considered ("generic") or only a specific alternative is considered ("specific").

docs.title: meaning
docs.text: Path to the csv file that defines the loci in which we want to look for SNVs.

docs.title: example
docs.text:
Entry in the config file:

calling_loci_list: home/files/calling_loci_list.csv

Where calling_loci_list.csv looks like this in the "generic" alt_mode:

"chrom","pos","ref"
"9",133748283,"C"
"9",133738363,"G"
"14",105246551,"C"
"2",29443695,"G"
"2",29432664,"C"
"X",47426121,"C"
"7",140453136,"A"
"7",55259515,"T"
"7",55249071,"C"

And like this in the "specific" alt_mode

"chrom","pos","ref","alt"
"9",133748283,"C","T"
"9",133738363,"G","A"
"14",105246551,"C","T"
"2",29443695,"G","T"
"2",29432664,"C","T"
"X",47426121,"C","G"
"7",140453136,"A","T"
"7",55259515,"T","G"
"7",55249071,"C","T"

docs.title: other considerations
docs.text: Note that the chromosome identifiers must match the ones used in the reference genome fasta file, to which your reads have been aligned. For example, if the reference uses a chr1 identifier for the 1st chromosome, then the same format needs to be used in your csv file.

docs.title: meaning
docs.text: FDR method, only applicable if the variant_calling_model is set to "binomial"

docs.title: meaning
docs.text: Path to the csv file containing the list of loci on which the error model will be fitted.

docs.title: example
docs.text:
Entry in the config file:

loci_list: home/files/loci_list.csv

Where loci_list.csv looks like this in the "generic" alt_mode:

"chrom","pos","ref"
"9",133748283,"C"
"9",133738363,"G"
"14",105246551,"C"
"2",29443695,"G"
"2",29432664,"C"
"X",47426121,"C"
"7",140453136,"A"
"7",55259515,"T"
"7",55249071,"C"

And like this in the "specific" alt_mode

"chrom","pos","ref","alt"
"9",133748283,"C","T"
"9",133738363,"G","A"
"14",105246551,"C","T"
"2",29443695,"G","T"
"2",29432664,"C","T"
"X",47426121,"C","G"
"7",140453136,"A","T"
"7",55259515,"T","G"
"7",55249071,"C","T"

docs.title: other considerations
docs.text: Note that the chromosome identifiers must match the ones used in the reference genome fasta file, to which your reads have been aligned. For example, if the reference uses a chr1 identifier for the 1st chromosome, then the same format needs to be used in your csv file.

docs.title: meaning
docs.text: Path to the text file that contains the path to the matched normal bam file.

docs.title: other considerations
docs.text:
The bam file must be sorted and indexed. See: 

https://www.htslib.org/doc/samtools-sort.html
https://www.htslib.org/doc/samtools-index.html

for more information.

docs.title: meaning
docs.text: During fitting of the error model, Epsilon tries to remove any mutated sites in order to isolate the error rate. In an attempt to achieve this, an upper bound is set on the observed variant allele fraction. The max_noise_level parameter defines this upperbound.

docs.title: meaning
docs.text: Path to the text file that contains the paths to the bam files that are part of the negative control cohort.

docs.title: meaning
docs.text: The number of parallel workers used to extract the features from the bam files that make up the negative control cohort.

docs.title: meaning
docs.text: Just the name of the output vcf, nothing less, nothing more.

docs.title: meaning
docs.text: The threshold on the posterior probability above which the variant is called.

docs.title: other considerations
docs.text: This parameter is only applicable when the if the variant_calling_model is set to "bayesian".

docs.title: meaning
docs.text: The prior probability of the given locus being mutated.

docs.title: other considerations
docs.text: This parameter is only applicable when the if the variant_calling_model is set to "bayesian".

docs.title: meaning
docs.text: Path to the reference genome fasta file.

docs.title: other considerations
docs.text:
The following supplementary files are needed:

Reference genome:
├── reference.fa
├── reference.fa.fai
├── reference.fa.amb
├── reference.fa.ann
├── reference.fa.bwt
├── reference.fa.pac
└── reference.fa.sa

See:

https://github.com/samtools/samtools
https://github.com/lh3/bwa
